sources.title: Microsoft Foundry
sources.shortSummary: Current Foundry resources can contain multiple projects; project assets include models, agents, tools and knowledge. The unit explicitly links the SDK for scripted asset management and CI/CD. Scope: current resource/project organization only, not classic hub architecture or universal availability of every new portal task.

sources.title: Explore the model catalog
sources.shortSummary: Use model cards and capability, inference-task and deployment filters to select models. Embeddings support similarity retrieval; image generation and visual understanding are different tasks. Scope: selection methodology; exclude mutable catalog totals, provider rankings and any implication that reasoning models expose hidden reasoning.

sources.title: Select models using benchmarks
sources.shortSummary: Compare task quality, safety, input/output cost and latency/throughput together. TTFT measures the first streamed token; tail percentiles describe slower requests. Scope: benchmark interpretation, not current leaderboard winners, benchmark question material or a guarantee of application performance.

sources.title: Deploy models to endpoints
sources.shortSummary: Deployment names route inference requests, model cards constrain supported deployment types, and managed compute requires suitable VM quota. The unit recommends Entra authentication for production. Scope: deployment planning; exclude universal residency claims, exact batch SLA/discount guarantees and support for an unverified model/type combination.

sources.title: Evaluate model performance
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes human evaluation, model-judged quality/safety metrics and reference-based NLP metrics. Evaluations can target models, agents or existing dataset outputs; repeat evaluations after changes. Scope: evaluation methodology and metric meanings, not proof that every named evaluator is GA or an approval of the withdrawn RAG evaluator article.

sources.title: Measure potential harms
sources.shortSummary: Define explicit harm criteria, establish a measured baseline and share results with stakeholders. Validate a small manual test set before scaling automation, then continue periodic manual checks. Scope: testing methodology only; exclude harmful example prompts and claims that automated scores prove safety.

sources.title: Manage a responsible generative AI solution
sources.shortSummary: Plan legal, privacy, security and accessibility prerelease reviews, phased delivery, incident response, rollback and feedback channels. Operational telemetry must follow privacy commitments. Scope: release and operating practices, not a documented automatic rollback API or permission to collect unrestricted user data.

sources.title: Understand AI agents and Microsoft Foundry Agent Service
sources.shortSummary: Agent risks include data leakage, prompt injection, excessive privilege, poisoned inputs, unsafe dependencies and unauditable actions. Mitigations include least privilege, validation, human approval and traceability. Scope: risk-control design; exclude blanket automatic execution of local functions, drift implementation details and new visual-workflow recommendations.

sources.title: Microsoft Foundry SDKs and endpoints
sources.shortSummary: Retains SDK/endpoint selection, current Python 2.x Stable/new Foundry versus 1.x classic, and scoped prerequisites/RBAC. Reviewed expanded scope covers AIProjectClient native setup/configuration, get_openai_client and the Python first Responses call through the project endpoint, plus direct resource /openai/v1 responsibilities and embedding routing. This is not an exclusive agent-management boundary, an SDK article agent_reference assertion, or blanket GA for every service, model or feature.

sources.title: Generate responses with the Responses API
sources.shortSummary: Responses can be chained with previous_response_id or an explicit message history. History, tools and retrieved content consume context tokens; streaming and async calls improve application responsiveness. Scope: demonstrated response-state patterns; exclude universal model support, unsupported sampling parameters and unbounded history-retention guarantees.

sources.title: Use the code\_interpreter tool
sources.shortSummary: The code_interpreter tool executes generated Python in a sandbox and can process files and inspect execution results. The lesson states no external network access and memory/time constraints. Scope: sandboxed computation versus retrieval or application-owned function execution; do not promise unrestricted packages, unlimited runtime or production correctness.

sources.title: Use the file\_search tool
sources.shortSummary: Upload and poll files into vector stores, supply vector_store_ids to file_search and include retrieval results for inspection. Retrieval quality depends on file quality and indexing freshness. Scope: bounded uploaded-file grounding; not a guarantee against fabrication or a substitute for enterprise knowledge-source governance.

sources.title: Use the function tool
sources.shortSummary: A model requests a function call; application code validates arguments, executes business logic and returns function_call_output with the matching call_id. Sensitive actions require authorization and logging. Scope: the developer-controlled execution contract, not automatic permission to run arbitrary model-selected code.

sources.title: Use function calling with Microsoft Foundry agents
sources.shortSummary: The current prompt-agent example declares a strict JSON-schema FunctionTool, handles function_call items in the application and returns FunctionCallOutput with matching call_id. The portal cannot edit function definitions. Scope: function lifecycle and Python prompt-agent contract; exclude the article's legacy run-expiry statement as a universal Responses API rule.

sources.title: Connect agents to Model Context Protocol servers
sources.shortSummary: Retains the reviewed baseline MCP connection, approval, untrusted-result and private-network scopes without blanket GA. Reviewed additional scope covers only the explicitly Preview long-running path: a tasks-capable remote server and related-task taskId, a background-capable model, Python background=True for an already configured named agent, and polling the response id while queued/in_progress. Preserve the distinction between task and response identifiers; no universal model support, polling SLA, terminal-error handling or ordinary-MCP Preview transfer is granted.

sources.title: Configure data sources for knowledge bases
sources.shortSummary: Choose existing Search indexes for custom search pipelines, remote SharePoint for live permission-aware queries, indexed SharePoint for preprocessed advanced search, and Blob/OneLake/Web for their respective content. Scope: documented source-selection tradeoffs, not absolute freshness, guaranteed response times or uniform feature availability.

sources.title: Configure retrieval with Foundry IQ
sources.shortSummary: Retrieval instructions should specify when to search, how to cite and what to do when evidence is absent. Test factual, synthesis, out-of-scope and ambiguous requests, then monitor citations, fallbacks and retrieval accuracy. Scope: instruction/test design; instructions do not technically guarantee retrieval or correct citations.

sources.title: Understand agent orchestration
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes sequential, concurrent, handoff, group-chat and manager-led orchestration; executors can be agents or custom logic and edges route messages. Scope: conceptual pattern selection and workflow-event purposes, not a promise that every listed event/class exists unchanged in every Agent Framework release.

sources.title: Use group chat orchestration
sources.shortSummary: A chat manager coordinates turn-based maker/checker critique and optional human involvement, including termination and next-speaker decisions. Scope: collaborative review and bounded discussion, not guaranteed correctness. Exclude the conflicting concurrent-execution implementation paragraph and unverified GroupChatBuilder API details.

sources.title: Prompt engineering techniques
sources.shortSummary: Use clear task instructions, few-shot examples, grounding context, output structure and explicit fallbacks. Tune temperature or top_p separately where supported. The article excludes reasoning models from these techniques and restricts hidden-reasoning extraction. Scope: non-reasoning model prompt design; exclude copied examples, guaranteed citation accuracy and tokenizer-generalization claims.

sources.title: System message design
sources.shortSummary: System messages specify assistant role, scope, output contract, safety constraints and fallback behavior. Test realistic and adversarial prompts and combine instructions with other controls. Scope: chat-based instruction design, not guaranteed compliance, guaranteed valid JSON or a multimodal safety implementation.

sources.title: Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) and indexes
sources.shortSummary: RAG retrieves content, augments the model input and generates an answer with source context. Indexing, chunking, access checks and token budgets affect quality, latency and exposure risk. Scope: RAG architecture versus behavior fine-tuning; grounding does not guarantee correctness and agentic-retrieval release status is not established by omission.

sources.title: Overview of Microsoft Foundry Models
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes models sold by Azure from partner/community offerings and managed compute from serverless deployment. Managed-compute models use classic hub-based projects and VM-hour billing; provider/model choices constrain deployment support. Scope: categories and tradeoffs; exclude catalog totals, universal SLAs, and instant access, which is explicitly preview.

sources.title: Test, deploy, and integrate agents
sources.shortSummary: Distinguishes saving an agent in a project from publishing a version to an Agent Application endpoint with its own identity. Reassign downstream roles to that identity; client-managed conversation history is required for the described stateless application endpoint. Scope: the lesson's preview application/hosted-agent flow, with release testing, backoff and monitoring; role names must be reconciled with current SDK documentation.

sources.title: Build a workflow in Microsoft Foundry (Preview)
sources.shortSummary: The visual workflow builder supports ordered nodes, branching, variables and human input, but does not support hosted agents in its designer. The article explicitly announces retirement on December 1, 2026 and recommends Agent Framework for new workflows. Scope: existing preview workflows and migration context, not recommended production architecture.

sources.title: Use workflows in code
sources.shortSummary: The lesson invokes a saved visual workflow by name through project conversations/Responses and distinguishes response.completed from individual output-item events. Scope: existing preview visual workflows only, jointly constrained by the approved workflow article's December 1, 2026 retirement; not a substitute for Agent Framework code.

sources.title: Develop a vision-based chat app
sources.shortSummary: The lesson contrasts Responses input_text/input_image parts with ChatCompletions text/image_url parts. Images can use a web URL or a MIME-correct Base64 data URL. Scope: the demonstrated multimodal request shapes, not image-detail budgets, maximum image counts or the withdrawn vision implementation article.

sources.title: Video generation with Sora 2 (preview)
sources.shortSummary: Sora 2 preview uses asynchronous creation, status retrieval and download, with reference-image and remix patterns. The current article states content restrictions including human-face reference rejection. Scope: lifecycle, reference/remix concepts and explicit preview status; exclude conflicting numeric duration/resolution/variant limits and blanket claims about all photorealistic content.

sources.title: What is Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools?
sources.shortSummary: API 2025-11-01 is the production GA baseline for multimodal extraction, analyzer schemas, structured JSON/Markdown and optional document-field confidence/grounding. API 2026-06-01-preview adds agentic mode, in-page segmentation, signature and metadata enhancements. Scope: explicitly distinguish those versions; confidence scores are not proof of accuracy or blanket support for every modality.

sources.title: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools document solutions
sources.shortSummary: Document analyzers combine content/layout extraction with typed extract, classify or generate fields. Enable confidence/grounding explicitly and route insufficiently supported results for human review. Scope: core extraction with the 2025-11-01 GA baseline from the approved overview; agentic mode and new signature/metadata capabilities are preview, not grandfathered GA.

sources.title: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools image solutions
sources.shortSummary: Image analyzers use a task-specific field schema to turn visual information into structured output for search or business workflows. The article recommends document field extraction when the primary task is text extraction from images. Scope: core image extraction under the approved overview's 2025-11-01 GA baseline, not guaranteed object detection accuracy.

sources.title: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools video solutions
sources.shortSummary: The current video article marks API 2026-06-01-preview, describes transcript/key-frame/segment output and schema-based custom metadata. Sampling around one frame per second and resized frames can miss brief events or small details; only speech is transcribed. Scope: this preview article, not universal video fidelity or permission to infer exact analyzer names from inconsistent examples.

sources.title: Azure Content Understanding in Foundry Tools audio solutions
sources.shortSummary: Conversational audio analyzers provide transcripts, diarization and schema-driven summaries/entities. Auto locale handling is multilingual only within supported combinations; explicit multiple locales select a dominant language. Scope: core 2025-11-01 audio extraction, supported also by the approved overview; avoid copying illustrative diarization outputs or interpreting latency labels as guarantees.

sources.title: Migrate from Azure Content Understanding Preview to GA
sources.shortSummary: The article identifies 2025-11-01 as GA, requires default model mappings, replaces Scenario with baseAnalyzerId, and makes document-field confidence/grounding opt-in. It distinguishes URL analyze requests from analyzeBinary and limits GA inputs to one item. Scope: GA migration; exclude preview-only features, the ambiguous base64 wording and stale GPT-4.1 requirements from older lessons.

sources.title: Azure Language tools and agents
sources.shortSummary: The Language MCP server, CLU/CQA intent-routing agent and exact-answer agent are explicitly preview. CLU classifies intent; CQA delivers curated answers, with optional RAG fallback. Scope: those integration distinctions and prerequisites; do not transpose the article's broad network caveat over the more specific current MCP private-endpoint requirements.

sources.title: Detect language
sources.shortSummary: Language detection returns per-document language identifiers and confidence. Mixed-language text may yield the dominant language with lower confidence; unparseable text can yield unknown. Scope: result interpretation, not rigid batch/character limits without API-version validation or a guarantee that every short input is recognized.

sources.title: Extract personally identifiable information (PII)
sources.shortSummary: PII recognition returns entity categories and confidence, while redacted_text provides a masked version of the input. Scope: detection versus redacted output and downstream privacy handling; sample entities and scores are illustrative, and automated redaction does not prove all sensitive information was removed.

sources.title: Translate text
sources.shortSummary: Translator supports text translation to one or more targets with optional source-language detection; transliteration changes the writing script rather than the language. Retrieve supported language lists instead of hard-coding counts. Scope: the shown text-client operations, not versionless claims for LLM translation, document preservation or all endpoints.

sources.title: Use the Speech to Text API
sources.shortSummary: SpeechConfig configures the resource and AudioConfig selects an input; SpeechRecognizer's single-utterance operation returns RecognizedSpeech, NoMatch or Canceled. Scope: the demonstrated SDK recognition flow, not continuous transcription, universal recognition accuracy or a claim that subscription keys are the only authentication method.

sources.title: Use Speech Synthesis Markup Language
sources.shortSummary: SSML controls pauses, phonemes, prosody, say-as interpretation, voices and supported speaking styles; send it with a speech synthesizer's SSML method. Scope: SSML intent and the shown request path, not a guarantee that every voice supports every style or the lesson's inconsistent narrator-name prose.

sources.title: Voice Live API for real-time voice agents
sources.shortSummary: Voice Live combines recognition, model interaction and synthesis over WebSocket events with optional interruption/turn handling and tools. Built-in models are managed, while BYOM models require deployment; custom voice/avatar access is limited. Scope: baseline architecture and pricing categories, not universal model availability, exact locale counts or GA for the explicitly preview Phi model.

sources.title: How to customize Voice Live input and output
sources.shortSummary: Phrase lists provide session-time recognition hints; custom_speech maps locales to model IDs and requires azure-speech with models on the same resource. A custom lexicon changes output pronunciation, not input recognition. Scope: input/output customization boundaries and eligibility constraints; exclude unreviewed personal-voice and avatar implementation details.

sources.title: Translate speech
sources.shortSummary: SpeechTranslationConfig and TranslationRecognizer produce target-language text. For multiple spoken targets, synthesize each translation separately; the lesson limits event-based synthesis to one target. Scope: those API roles and translation patterns; do not reuse the sample's event-file overwrite behavior or unverified Python AudioConfig alias.

sources.title: Extract data with an indexer
sources.shortSummary: An indexer can crack source documents, build an enrichment tree, apply OCR to normalized images, merge extracted text and map outputs into index fields. Scope: pull-based enrichment and field mappings, not a claim that all indexes must be populated by indexers or that schema defaults apply to every API.

sources.title: Add a custom skill to an Azure AI Search enrichment pipeline
sources.shortSummary: A custom Web API skill exchanges values arrays whose data records are correlated by recordId; code runs outside Search. HTTPS, bounded timeouts and matching authResourceId/endpoint identities matter. Scope: documented interface and managed-identity prerequisites; API key examples are not a recommendation to expose secrets.

sources.title: Querying in Azure AI Search
sources.shortSummary: Full-text queries search tokenized text, vector queries search embeddings and hybrid requests combine both. OData filters act on filterable values without lexical analysis; document lookup retrieves a key directly. Scope: baseline query distinctions; agentic-retrieval lifecycle labels conflict with the current architecture page and require separate resolution.

sources.title: Filters for keyword search in Azure AI Search
sources.shortSummary: OData filters qualify nonvector filterable fields and can accompany full-text or vector requests. Literal string matching is case-sensitive by default, with normalizers as an exception; existing field filterability requires a new field or rebuild. Scope: filtering behavior, not the malformed example string or an assertion that all vector filters run before search.

sources.title: What is the Document Intelligence layout model?
sources.shortSummary: The explicit v4.0/2024-11-30 GA layout section uses prebuilt-layout for OCR and document structure, including paragraph roles, tables, figures and Markdown output. Office embedded images and XLSX table analysis are unsupported. Scope: this v4 section, with file/tier constraints; exclude retiring monikers and inconsistent legacy JSON-container prose.

sources.title: Create a Content Understanding analyzer
sources.shortSummary: Custom analyzers declare baseAnalyzerId, fieldSchema, extraction intent and model mappings. SDK creation returns a poller; REST creation uses PUT and an Operation-Location status URL. Scope: analyzer-definition structure and asynchronous lifecycle; exclude placeholder Python syntax, busy polling and obsolete model deployment prerequisites.

sources.title: Analyze content
sources.shortSummary: Analysis identifies an analyzer and accepts URL inputs or a separate analyzeBinary operation. SDK poller.result waits for completion; successful results contain fields, Markdown and source structure. Scope: request/result separation, not unconditional success, safe production polling code or default confidence/grounding availability.

sources.title: Compare and combine optimization strategies
sources.shortSummary: Prompting guides behavior, RAG supplies current/private context and fine-tuning improves consistent task behavior; they can be combined incrementally. Scope: choosing complementary optimization strategies, not fixed cost rankings, guaranteed accuracy or the false implication that prompt-supplied context cannot add new information.

sources.title: Content filtering for Microsoft Foundry Models (classic)
sources.shortSummary: The article applies only to Foundry classic. It documents input image/text harm filtering, distinct prompt-attack controls, annotation versus blocking, and filtered completion handling. Scope: classic baseline controls; exclude embeddings/audio, current-portal steps, universal custom-policy detection and any doc-to-doc approval of withdrawn Prompt Shields.

sources.title: What is Azure AI Search?
sources.shortSummary: Classic Search accepts pushed JSON or pull-indexed content and returns ranked documents; agentic retrieval targets knowledge bases with planning and structured references. The comparison explicitly marks classic GA and some agentic capabilities preview. Scope: classic ingestion/query architecture and Dedicated scaling; Serverless Developer is explicitly preview and not transferable to other tiers.

sources.title: What is Azure Speech?
sources.shortSummary: Speech distinguishes live, fast prerecorded and asynchronous batch transcription, synthesis, translation and custom speech for domain/acoustic needs. Scope: capability selection; LLM speech is explicitly preview, language/region support varies, and custom voice carries separate responsible-use restrictions.

sources.title: Mitigate potential harms
sources.shortSummary: Layer harm mitigations across model choice, platform safety controls, prompts/grounding and user experience, then retest against the measured baseline. Scope: the four-layer methodology only; exclude the lesson's conflation of task adherence with four-level harm categories and do not treat a named capability as a linked product document.

sources.title: What are image-generation models?
sources.shortSummary: Image-generation models synthesize graphical output from natural-language descriptions rather than retrieving pictures from a curated catalog. The unit identifies text-to-image model discovery. Scope: generation versus search and input/output modality, not pixel controls, guaranteed originality, model availability or the withdrawn image how-to.

sources.title: Enrich extracted data with AI skills
sources.shortSummary: An enrichment skillset can add language, entity, key-phrase, translation, PII, OCR and image-description outputs; custom skills wrap external processing into new fields. Scope: skill purposes and custom enrichment architecture only; exclude the unit's unqualified regional, free-document and execution-order claims.

sources.title: Search an index
sources.shortSummary: Index field attributes distinguish keys, searchable text, filterable constraints, sortable values, facets and retrievable results; select controls returned fields. Scope: those attributes and facet/sort intent only. Exclude the lesson's invalid simple-filter example, restriction of OData filters to full syntax, and unqualified TF/IDF ranking claim.

sources.title: Create a Content Understanding analyzer
sources.shortSummary: A Content Understanding workflow defines a content-specific schema, tests it against samples, builds an analyzer and refines named versions. Templates and fields depend on input modality. Scope: schema/test/build lifecycle and Studio role, not automatic resource-provisioning guarantees or uniformly available fields across modalities.

sources.title: Explore image-generation models in Microsoft Foundry portal
sources.shortSummary: The current training unit uses a Foundry project's Images playground to submit prompts and inspect generated images. Output size and reference-image controls are explicitly subject to model support. Scope: those model-dependent playground controls only; no universal dimensions, mask/edit/streaming API contract or affirmative model GA lifecycle.

sources.title: Create a client application that uses an image generation model
sources.shortSummary: The unit demonstrates client.images.generate with a model deployment, prompt and image settings, followed by Base64 decoding of data[0].b64_json and writing image bytes in binary mode. Scope: the illustrated Images API request/result flow; the sample does not prove every model supports its n/size values, does not supply a full authenticated client, and does not establish image editing, streaming or GA lifecycle.

sources.title: Use the Text to Speech API
sources.shortSummary: SpeechConfig configures the service while the audio output configuration selects a speaker, file or application-handled audio result. SpeechSynthesizer performs synthesis; the Python example distinguishes SynthesizingAudioCompleted from Canceled and inspects cancellation_details. Scope: the documented output destination and success/cancellation flow, not input recognition, complete SDK version/lifecycle proof or unshown constructor variants.

sources.title: Configure audio format and voices
sources.shortSummary: The unit separates the synthesis output format, selected with set_speech_synthesis_output_format, from the named voice selected with speech_synthesis_voice_name. Format choices concern file type, sample rate and bit depth. Scope: those independent configuration responsibilities and shown examples; no claim that a filename determines encoding, every voice supports every feature, or the linked SDK/language pages are newly approved.

sources.title: Transcribe speech
sources.shortSummary: The audio transcription unit demonstrates AzureOpenAI with api_version 2025-03-01-preview, uploading an audio file to audio.transcriptions.create and requesting text output. It explicitly says model availability varies by region. Scope: this preview-version example and transcription versus synthesis; it does not prove every listed model accepts every response format or establish current regional deployments, GA status or a new approval for the linked model catalog article.

sources.title: Synthesize speech
sources.shortSummary: The synthesis unit demonstrates AzureOpenAI with api_version 2025-03-01-preview, text input, a voice and instructions passed to audio.speech.with_streaming_response.create, then writes the response with stream_to_file. Model availability varies by region. Scope: this preview-version streamed-audio example; the output_speech.wav suffix does not establish WAV encoding because the sample sets no response_format, and no model/region matrix or linked document is newly approved.

sources.title: Use the Azure OpenAI Responses API
sources.shortSummary: Retains the previously scoped Responses baseline without blanket GA. Reviewed additional scope is ONLY the stored Python nonstreaming image_generation example: explicit preview header, separate image-deployment and outer model bindings, and type-filtered Base64 image results. All streaming/multiturn contradictions and old exclusions remain; no automatic Preview transfer to other APIs, model/region/format guarantees, filename-to-encoding inference, or doc-to-doc permission is granted.

sources.title: Extract entities
sources.shortSummary: The current entity lesson demonstrates per-document recognize_entities results using doc.id, entity.text and entity.category, and directly identifies the named-entity-categories article. Scope: the illustrated entity extraction and category interpretation only. Do not infer exact SDK/API GA, offsets, error schemas, custom NER or compatibility with the newer GA API type/Subcategory change.

sources.title: Named entity categories and types
sources.shortSummary: Contains affirmative Stable: Generally Available wording for the named NER API and states that the GA API released 2024-11-01 replaces Subcategory classifications with type. Scope: that explicitly qualified NER API/type contract and unambiguous listed types. Exclude the inconsistent URL/Skill and Geological/Geographical rows and mismatched Preview link; do not transfer GA or field compatibility to old SDK code, PII, detection, Translator or linked documents.

sources.title: Azure Language in Microsoft Foundry Tools
sources.shortSummary: The service lesson configures TextAnalyticsClient at the Foundry resource endpoint with AzureKeyCredential or DefaultAzureCredential and recommends Entra for production. It labels sentiment, summarization and key-phrase capabilities deprecated for existing applications. Scope: these resource-client examples and that limited note, not blanket API GA, project-key compatibility, replacement/retirement schedules or permission to cite the external PyPI link.

sources.title: Connect and use the Language MCP server with an agent
sources.shortSummary: Only the unit's positive/negative review-attitude prose is approved: it identifies that assessment as sentiment analysis alongside entity recognition. The shown Language MCP endpoint explicitly uses 2025-11-15-preview. Exclude the contradictory detect_language_from_text-for-sentiment tool pair and every SDK, dispatch, output-schema or borrowed per-operation lifecycle claim. This scoped source approval does not reverse a prior question hold.

sources.title: Explore the AI Voice Live client library for Python
sources.shortSummary: The unit explicitly describes the Voice Live Python SDK as async-only as of version 1.0.0, deprecates synchronous use, names event roles and requires immediate client-side playback cancellation on interruption. Scope: those version-qualified statements and local responsibility only; no blanket GA, exact import guarantee, runtime audio type, complete cancellation/flush implementation or concurrency contract. Source Not applicable does not waive software lifecycle evidence.

sources.title: Create a Voice Live agent
sources.shortSummary: The unit explicitly shows a 2026-01-01-preview Voice Live agent-mode connection and separation of stored agent/session settings from client audio input/output. Its metadata example uses azure-speech input transcription and an Azure-standard output voice. Scope: that illustrated Preview connection/configuration separation only; custom_speech, phrase_list and custom_lexicon_url are absent and not admitted. Preserve code-order, import, residual-buffer, ID/name and numeric-limit exclusions; no whole executable-client or general lifecycle guarantee.
